who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), executor of track 5 T1 (the idle budget), int-1112
what: Counting kept front ends (so the process tables are freed only once none is) needs a Drop on KeptLowered, but `lower` took a kept front end apart by a struct pattern, which a Drop type forbids; and the take is not a drop of the database, only its end as a kept one. KeptLowered became a counted holder of KeptParts (Deref), taken apart by into_parts, which ends the count. Separately: an idle daemon held to 48 MiB with something it may not give (a floor in its wait, a live image) would have listed and purged every 250 ms forever, since the allocator's estimate never falls; it now plans again only after the budget's wait.
cost: a redesign of the kept front end's type in the middle of a memory task
cause: the kept front end's lifetime (kept, taken, dropped) was implicit in moves, with no type marking where it ends
class: a resource whose end is a move, not a drop, so no hook sees it
prevention: a holder type whose every way out (drop, take) is one method that says what ends
fix: KeptLowered::{new, into_parts, Drop}; giving.rs backs an idle plan off by idle::BUDGET_AFTER
